newsitem.title: UK: Calm mark ticks up vs peseta on Spanish rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Calm mark ticks up vs peseta on Spanish rate cut.

text.p: The mark inched up against the peseta in European morning trade after a Spanish rate cut which had been anticipated by the market, while the mark crosses were otherwise calm.

The mark edged up to 84.38/40 pesetas from 84.34/36 earlier, after the Bank of Spain announced it cut its key money rate by 5.25 percent from 5.50 at today's regular repo tender. Mark/peseta was at 84.37/40 in late European trade on Thursday.
Analysts had forecast a 25 basis point cut in the repo rate after Spain unveiled mild consumer price inflation data on Wednesday.
"This isn't going to have much of an impact, the rate cut was built into it. They (Spain) aren't going to do anything else for a while," said a trader at Standard Chartered.
Analysts said it would be difficult for Spain to lower rates aggressively from here, noting that today's repo rate cut was its fourth one this year.

"Spain's got a bit more mileage to cut rates but it will be much more difficult to do it aggressively as rates have come down a long way in the past 18 months," said Ken Wattret, international economist at Banque Paribas here.

"Inflation is also pivotal. Recently the decline in inflation has been precipitous, and although May CPI will again be supportive, from the middle of the year we'll probably see an upward trend," Wattret said.
Mark/escudo firmed briefly, with traders saying it was pulled up in sympathy with mark/peseta.

But they said a bigger reason for the escudo's softness was a strengthening in expectations Portugal would join European monetary union at its launch in 1999. The mark rose to a high of 100.92 escudos and eased to 100.74/77, against its late Thursday level of 100.84/87. It hit a 1997 high of 100.94 yesterday.

Speculation that Portugal would be one of the first-wave EMU members heightened this week after EU finance ministers on Monday praised the country's economic convergence plans to qualify for the single currency.

Traders said this has led the market to push the escudo towards its central rate of 102.50 per mark in the European exchange rate mechanism in the growing belief the central rates will be the conversion rates into the euro.
"I don't think the escudo's going to drop very far against the mark. Judging from fundamentals, the escudo's still a buy," said one trader at a Japanese bank.

"Certainly the comments we've had from the European Commission in the past month tell us one thing, and that is that Spain's and Portugal's prospects of making EMU's first wave has greatly increased," Paribas' Wattret said.
"On the basis of that scenario continuing, we would see the escudo performing well," he said.

Elsewhere, mark/French franc was a touch lower at 3.3675/78 against Thursday's 3.3681/86. The latest Ipsos poll showed the ruling coalition was expected to win 323 seats in the May 25/June 1 National Assembly election compared with 293 for the opposition left-wing.
Mark/lira was at 985.50/70 against Thursday's 986.85/15. Mark/Swiss slid to 84.07 centimes, its lowest since November 12 last year, from 84.45/47 yesterday.
